metas.name: Czechia - Bicycle signs
metas.note: Bicycle signs in Czechia are yellow.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Czechia - Black Sign Caps
metas.note: Czech sign posts typically have thick, black caps.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Czechia - Directional Signs
metas.note:
Czechia uses arrow-shaped directional signs with a filled in tip. Due to the shape, they are recognizable from behind.

NOTE: Slovakia has small white arrows instead.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Czechia - Gen 2 Coverage
metas.note:
While rare, it is possible to find Generation 2 in Czechia.

NOTE: Slovakia does not have any Generation 2.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Czechia - Gen 3 Coverage
metas.note:
Much of Czech Generation 3 coverage was taken during winter, resulting in very grey, and occasionally snowy, coverage.

NOTE: This is not common in Slovakia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Czechia - Highway Signs
metas.note:
Czech highway signs can be either blue or green, and have a thin white border, which is separated from the edge by a second coloured border.

NOTE: Slovak highway signs have a white border right on the edge.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Czechia - House Numbers
metas.note: House numbers in Czechia are generally written on blue or red signs with thin white borders.
metas.footer: Plonk it Czechia, Plonk it Slovakia

metas.name: Czechia - Kilometre Markers
metas.note: Czech kilometre markers have a yellow outline outside the black frame and do not have a black horizontal middle line.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Czechia - Ř, Ě and Ů
metas.note: Czech distinctly uses the letters Ř, Ě and Ů. NOTE: Acute accents on vowels are not found in South Slavic languages.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Czechia - Railway Crossing
metas.note: Czech railway crossing signs do not have a background.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Czechia - Road Signs
metas.note:
The borders of Czech road signs are almost always separated from the edge by a strip in the same colour as the sign background.

NOTE: In Slovakia, it is more common for signs to have the border on the edge of the sign.
metas.footer: Plonk it Czechia, Plonk it Slovakia

metas.name: Czechia - Roadlines
metas.note:
Czechia often has solid outer roadlines, with no centre line.

NOTE: While these roadlines can be found in all neighbouring countries, it is notably also common in Germany.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Czechia - Rolling Hills
metas.note: The Czech landscape is fairly rolling, with a lot of hills and altitude changes, but not a lot of tall mountains. Generally speaking, Slovakia has more mountains, but also more completely flat areas.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Czechia - Split Houses
metas.note:
Suburban houses in Czechia are commonly connected in pairs.

NOTE: This is less common in most neighbouring countries, including Slovakia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Czechia - Street Signs
metas.note: In Czechia, street signs are typically bright red —either wide and wall-mounted or thin and on posts. Blue variants are also common. The Czech word for street is “ulice” (not “ulica”), though it's often omitted. In contrast, Slovakia uses white signs with red borders and blue text.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/czechia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Bold Font
metas.note: Slovak road signs normally feature a very bold font.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Concrete Pole Support
metas.note: Wooden poles and white concrete supports are more common in Slovakia than in Czechia. However, due to variability, this detail is preferably used for tough 50/50 decisions.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Directional Signs
metas.note: Slovakia uses blue directional signs, with small white arrows.
metas.footer: Plonk it Czechia, Plonk it Slovakia

metas.name: Slovakia - Double Posts
metas.note:
It is fairly common to see small signs with double sign posts in Slovakia.

NOTE: While large signs may have double sign posts, small signs rarely do in Czechia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Grey Metall Roof
metas.note:
Grey metal roofs are very common, particularly in the eastern parts of Slovakia.

NOTE: Apart from the most mountainous areas, it is far less common in Czechia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Highway Signs
metas.note: Slovak highway signs can be either blue or green, and have a white border right at the edge of the sign.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovakia - House Numbers
metas.note: House numbers in Slovakia are typically written on white signs with a thin red or black border.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Kilometre Markers
metas.note: Slovak kilometre markers typically have two sections divided with a black horizontal line. The top section contains the road number.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Ľ, Ô, Ä, Ŕ and Ĺ
metas.note: Slovakia distinctly uses the letters Ľ, Ô, Ä, Ŕ and Ĺ.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovakia - New Bollards
metas.note: Slovakia recently adopted a new bollard design similar to Hungary’s: a wedge-shaped European style with a red front reflector. Currently, it's still rarely seen.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Railway Crossing
metas.note: The Slovak railway crossing sign has a white rectangular background.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Road Signs
metas.note: Slovak road signs commonly have the painted sign border right at the edge of the sign.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Slovakia Sign Cap
metas.note: The top of Slovak sign posts are typically either open, have a grey metal cap or a thin black cap.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Street Signs
metas.note: White street signs with blue text and a thin red border are by far the most common in Slovakia.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.

metas.name: Slovakia - Very Flat/Mountainous
metas.note: The Slovak landscape varies between very mountainous and completely flat. Generally speaking, Czechia is hillier, but less mountainous.
metas.footer: Description and images taken from: www.plonkit.net/slovakia.
